profile.headline: Hardware & Software Engineer -  focusing on VR, AR, & IoT custom ASIC designs.
profile.jobTitle: Hardware & Software Engineer - Embedded design for VR/AR applications
profile.summary:
Interested in multimedia platforms for 3D virtual worlds and applications which require 3D rendering/modeling resources. Hardware interfaces of interest include the Cyberith gaming platform, the Oculus Rift, the PrioVR system (17 sensor Pro Developer Suit), and the Leap Motion VR developer tools. Unity 3D and the Unreal gaming engine are also areas of recent study. Java multimedia applications are interest, especially those which use advanced 3D modeling/rendering technologies. Java technologies of interest include J2SE, J2ME, Java3D, JINI, JMF, Android, & JavaFX. Currently using Xcode, Eclipse, Atmel Studio, Qt, and Netbeans IDEs for development. 

I develop virtual world content and software for HighFidelity.io, Second Life, and OpenSim. I recently installed source code for the HighFidelity project and plan to get more involved in related development projects. I have experience building and configuring OpenSim servers on Ubuntu Linux, Mac OS-X,  & Windows platforms. I am also interested in porting OpenSim to ARM based platforms. My VR servers are currently running on Via Technologies Mini-ITX cards and Nvidia Jetson cards. My focus is to develop a small VR appliance (VRMAD) that includes preconfigured environments that require very little configuration input from the end users. Leveraging embedded Java solutions using chips from aJile Systems, Yost Labs, Nvidia, and Imsys Technologies.

I have extensive experience porting applications to Mac OS-X, Windows, and various Linux platforms. My broad exposure to operating systems includes; Mac OS-X, Fedora, Ubuntu, Mint, CentOS, Android, Chrome OS, Solaris 10.  I typically use Java, C, C++, and some TCL/TK & Qt for development projects. Considering Swift for iOS applications.

positions.title: Hardware & Software Engineer - Embedded design for VR/AR applications
positions.description: Pursuing AR/VR/IoT development projects.See samples of my virtual worlds on Sansar.com (Drifter's Desire) or Opensim based projects on OSGrid (Regions: Banshee Cove or Epicenter Technologies). I design custom VR worlds on Second Life, Opensim, Sansar, and High Fidelity. In addition to virtual world design, I am also developing a new VR hardware platform and a library of software APIs for Nvidia Jetson TX2 cards.  Several VR related peripherals and hardware interfaces are in development now. The intent is to develop interfaces that allow you to control real world devices from within a virtual space. IoT devices with a VR spin!

positions.title: R&D Manager - Engineering
positions.description: Developed a wide range of embedded devices in support of various R&D and product development projects. I also designed advanced software applications using C, C++, Java, Labview, and MySQL that ran on a wide range of computing platforms. I have experience taking complex products from concept through production using off-shore and US based contract manufacturing resources.  Currently developing hardware at the system, board, FPGA, and chip levels. Other responsibilities included patent applications, network design/support, component purchasing, reverse engineering, competitive analysis, and technical staffing.

positions.title: Sr. Engineer
positions.description: Was a senior engineer responsible for device/process modeling, process characterization, standard cell development, and CMOS design methodologies. Used BSIM Pro for semiconductor device modeling and Cadence VSDE/VCME for timing characterization. Developed the CMOS standard cell family that was being used for ink jet print head development. The cells were compatible with the Cadence Encounter place and route system and support Synopsys and Xilinx flows for synthesis. The cells were also ported to the Tanner place and route tools. Used the Coventor SEMulator3D tools for device structure and standard cell analysis. Participated in RCX/QRC correlation activities using parasitic extraction structures and various circuits for digital performance analysis. Was also responsible for parametric process analysis and monitoring using Spotfire/JMP data analysis software, ChipCentric, and custom Process Control Monitor structures. The group I worked in was part of the Lexmark Imaging Solutions and Services R&D Group which was responsible for new ink jet print head designs and systems.

positions.title: Founder
positions.description: Designed a Java based broadband multimedia VR platform and teamed with five partners to pursue venture capital funding for the project. Developed the business plan, product specifications, technical presentations, and marketing support material. Conducted research on product components, Java processors, software APIs, manufacturing resources, and competing technologies. Developed and submitted patent applications and support material as needed. Made the hardware architecture for the VR platform public after development funds were exhausted. (See http://vrmad.epicentertech.com for additional information)

positions.title: Engineering Manager
positions.description: Engineering Manager of ADTRAN's mixed-signal IC development group. Responsibilities at ADTRAN included management of 3rd party mixed-signal design activities, semiconductor foundry procurement, IC design methodologies, EDA tool support, and the development of mixed-signal test systems. I also participated in the development of DDS, ISDN, T1/E1, MDSL, SDSL, HDSL-2, and G.SHDSL transceivers. Designs were implemented using CMOS technologies (MOSIS, AMI, NWL, UMC, & TSMC). Foundry procurement activities included a survey of vendors for 0.35u, 0.25u, 0.18u, and 0.15-0.10u CMOS and BICMOS technologies.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description: Worked as an independent consultant providing EDA services, UNIX support, software development services, and web related design services (C++ CGI, Java, & HTML). Customers included Advanced Microelectronics, ADTRAN, ATSI (ISP related), and a secure government agency

positions.title: CAD Section Manager - DOD Program Mgr
positions.description: My responsibilities included CAD tool integration, custom application development, laboratory automation, and Sun network operations. In addition, I was responsible for a team of engineers that developed custom CAD software and integrated circuits for various government agencies. The tools developed by this team (CMOSX cell library) were distributed to over 300 universities and research organizations. I was directly responsible for program proposals that resulted in $9.7 million in new funding for our division. Under these programs I managed teams of 8-14 engineers depending on the nature of the project.

positions.title: Semiconductor Device Modeling Engineer
positions.description: Employed as a Device Modeling Engineer developing circuit simulation models for CMOS and BIPOLAR devices. Modeling activities were supported by IEEE-488 software driving parametric test equipment from a Vax 11/780 and a Macintosh II. I was responsible for the definition and development of the entire system including low level hardware interfaces. Semiconductor characterization routines were developed using LabView instrument control software and Lightspeed C. Statistical process control databases were implemented on the Macintosh and were used to determine the upper and lower bounds for various device models. Parameter optimization algorithms were used to fit the models to empirical data.

positions.title: Section Manager - Design Systems Engineering
positions.description: As Section Manager of the Design Systems Engineering Group I directed the development of software systems which provided interfaces to Mentor CAD tools. I was also responsible for the acquisition, maintenance, and support of all workstation hardware and software. While at TRW I developed systems to monitor semiconductor wafer processing, parameter optimization software for circuit simulation, and simulator interfaces to schematic databases. Applications and simulation models were developed using C, Pascal, Modula-2 and Fortran. In addition, I provided technical support with logic simulation tools, block place and route software, and silicon compilers.

positions.title: Digital CMOS Design Engineer
positions.description: Hired as a start-up member of the MEC gate array design team participating in all phases of gate array and standard cell design. Primarily involved in CAD tool development, logic cell design, and digital system modeling. The gate-array masters developed by our group were marketed by Intersil, a GE subsidiary. Also worked in the GE CMOS Advance IC Development Group (Lynchburg VA). Responsibilities included characterization of short channel CMOS processes, standard cell development, and logic verification of digital subsystems for mobile phones, pagers, and radios.

projects.title: VR Sensor/IO Module
projects.description: The goal of this project is to develop interfaces that allow your virtual world objects to control real world objects, systems, & processes. The module will also allow you to create in-world displays of real time data , video content, and 3D models. It will be a stand-alone embedded device that works with a range of VR platforms and supports standard wireless protocols.

projects.title: Adaptive VR realtime rendering  cluster
projects.description: Leverage parallel computing algorithms to adapt real time rendering quality to the rotational and linear movement of a avatar in a VR scene graph. Using the Parallella 16 core Epiphany RISC SOC and a Xilinx Zynq FPGA (dual A9 ARM cores) to test various algorithms.
